proposal.title: Does Per-Fault Mitigation Already Catch Cascades? A Controlled Comparison of Cascade-Aware Attribution vs. Pinned Per-Fault Baselines on CPU Workflows
proposal.research_question: On independently authored CPU workflow episodes containing two or more co-occurring or cascading tool faults, does a cascade-aware attribution gate change the correct-completion rate relative to a pinned per-fault injection-and-mitigation baseline, and does any change survive when the label-generating oracle is removed from the gate's reach and a no-gate control is added?
proposal.hypothesis: Any correct-completion advantage of cascade-aware attribution over a pinned per-fault baseline will be small and will shrink toward zero once (a) the gate cannot query the reference evaluator at inference time and (b) a no-gate and a provenance-contract-only control are included; the per-fault baseline is expected to already catch a substantial fraction of cascades via dependency invalidation.
method_steps: Define two CPU workflow families with deterministic reference evaluators and explicit tool dependency DAGs: (F1) multi-step tabular transform with dependent tool calls; (F2) retrieve-then-aggregate with chained evidence dependencies. Each family has its own independently authored episode set and its own evaluator; no episode or evaluator is shared across families.

Author episodes in three strata per family: clean (valid inputs, valid updates), single-fault, and compound-fault (>=2 injected faults, at least one cascading through a dependency edge). Ground-truth completion labels are produced by the family evaluator, which is a separate process from any gate and is never exposed to the gate at inference time.

Pin the primary baseline to the published AgentCheck configuration (arxiv:2607.11098v1) as described in its setup section; if the published configuration cannot be reproduced exactly, run both the published-configuration re-implementation and a from-scratch re-implementation and report both, labeled.

Implement four conditions as separate adapters over the same episode runner: (A) no-gate control; (B) provenance-contract-only control (selective invalidation, no attribution rule); (C) pinned per-fault injection + mitigation baseline; (D) cascade-aware attribution gate. All four share the same cached initial model outputs per episode; only recovery calls differ.

Enforce oracle separation: the gate process receives only episode inputs, tool outputs, and the dependency DAG. The evaluator runs in a separate process after the episode ends. A pre-registered static check verifies the gate module has no import path or file handle to the evaluator.

Add a trivial-evaluator control as a pre-registered condition: replace the evaluator with a constant-label rule and confirm the gate's measured benefit collapses, which would indicate evaluator-side leakage rather than genuine attribution.
Tune thresholds only on the development split; freeze them; run once on the held-out split. Report per-family results separately, never pooled.

Count API calls per episode, per condition, and per baseline, decomposed into cached-initial calls (shared across conditions) and online recovery calls (condition-specific). Report wall-clock and token cost with uncertainty intervals.
Run a pre-registered power analysis on development-split variance before any margin claim; if the required N exceeds budget, report the study as underpowered rather than claiming an effect.

baselines.name: Pinned per-fault injection + mitigation (AgentCheck published configuration, arxiv:2607.11098v1)
baselines.why_strong: Directly matches the closest published setup, including paired clean/injected/mitigation runs with cached tool results; if it already catches cascades via its mitigation step, the cascade-aware gate adds nothing.

baselines.name: Provenance-contract-only control (selective invalidation, Matrix-style, arxiv:2608.12761v1)
baselines.why_strong: Represents the strongest existing structural-integrity approach and can catch cascades through dependency invalidation without any attribution rule, isolating whether attribution adds value beyond invalidation.

baselines.name: No-gate control
baselines.why_strong: Establishes the floor: how often the underlying agent completes correctly on compound-fault episodes with no mitigation at all, so any gate benefit is measured against the true baseline rather than against another gate.

task_families: F1: multi-step tabular data-transformation workflow with dependent tool calls and a deterministic recomputation evaluator
F2: retrieve-then-aggregate workflow with chained evidence dependencies and a deterministic aggregation evaluator
experiment.unit_of_analysis: One episode (one workflow run on one input) with a binary correct-completion label from the family evaluator, plus per-episode API-call and wall-clock counts.
experiment.development_split: Episodes used only for threshold and rule tuning; never used for reported margins.
experiment.held_out_split: Pre-registered episodes never inspected during development; run once after thresholds are frozen.
experiment.primary_metric: Correct-completion rate on compound-fault episodes, reported per family with confidence intervals.
secondary_metrics: API calls per episode (cached-initial vs. online recovery, per condition)
experiment.independent_reference: A deterministic family evaluator that recomputes the correct final artifact from the input and tool specifications, running in a separate process from the gate and never queryable by it at inference time.
experiment.normal_case_control: Clean episodes with valid inputs and valid updates; overblocking is measured as false-block rate, and the no-gate control establishes the clean-episode completion ceiling.

response_to_critique.change: Reframed the contribution as an empirical comparison answering a specific operational question (does per-fault mitigation already catch cascades?) rather than an algorithmic-novelty claim; the title and research question now state this directly.

Pinned the primary baseline to the published AgentCheck configuration and added a rule that if exact reproduction fails, both the published-configuration re-implementation and a from-scratch re-implementation are run and reported separately.

Added explicit oracle separation: the gate process cannot import or read the evaluator, verified by a pre-registered static check; the trivial-evaluator control is now a pre-registered condition, not a post-hoc check.

API calls are now decomposed into cached-initial (shared across conditions) and online recovery (condition-specific) calls, reported per episode, per condition, and per baseline, with uncertainty intervals and a pre-registered power analysis before any margin claim.
Two independent task families with independently authored episodes and separate evaluators; per-family results are reported separately and never pooled.
Added a no-gate control and a provenance-contract-only control to isolate the attribution rule from both the evaluator and from existing invalidation mechanisms.

falsification_conditions: Cascade-aware gate does not exceed the pinned per-fault baseline on held-out compound-fault episodes by the pre-registered margin, per family.
False-block rate on clean episodes exceeds the pre-registered bound.
Benefit collapses under the trivial-evaluator control, indicating evaluator-side leakage.
Benefit disappears when the provenance-contract-only control is included, indicating the attribution rule adds nothing beyond existing invalidation.
Pre-registered power analysis shows the study is underpowered to detect the pre-registered margin.
limitations: Novelty is unestablished; the closest ACM full text remains unavailable and no novelty conclusion is permitted.
Compound-fault episodes may still exhibit floor or ceiling effects; the previous pilot's 1/24 exact accuracy is a warning, not a resolved issue.
The pinned baseline may not be exactly reproducible from the published description; both variants will be reported but neither is guaranteed to match the original.
Results are development-handoff only and do not support generalization, significance, or causal claims.
CPU-only workflows may not transfer to tool-rich or GPU-dependent agent settings.
remaining_literature_checks: Full-text comparison against AgentCheck (arxiv:2607.11098v1) setup section to confirm the exact published baseline configuration and whether its mitigation step already handles cascades.
Full-text comparison against Matrix (arxiv:2608.12761v1) selective invalidation and bounded recovery to confirm the provenance-contract-only control is not a strawman.
Targeted search for any published compound/cascading tool-fault benchmark with independently authored episodes and operational cost reporting.
Check whether any prior work already reports a no-gate and provenance-contract-only control on compound-fault episodes, which would pre-empt the comparison.

sources.finding: Algorithm 1 changes one cached tool response. Section 6 explicitly excludes evaluation of compound and cascading failures. Retry/schema/filter wrappers are examined; this is not a published dependency-invalidation baseline.
sources.consequence: Compound-fault study remains a possible empirical extension. Do not claim to reproduce a pinned AgentCheck configuration: no exact implementation/configuration has been obtained for this project.

sources.finding: Selective recovery already follows transitive declared dependencies after version changes. Full rerun is a strong safe alternative when lineage is unavailable. Contracts and declared dependencies can themselves be incomplete.
sources.consequence: The proposed cascade-aware adapter must differ operationally from selective invalidation or be described as a replication/empirical extension. Compare to full replay with matched information and budgets.

sources.finding: AgentProp-Bench studies parameter injection and propagation with simulated tools. Its interceptor combines schema/error checks, uncertainty keywords and numerical consistency; the paper separates judge validation from task outcomes.
sources.code_access: Repository landing page opened; source not yet pinned or reproduced.
sources.consequence: Propagation plus a schema interceptor is already prior work. Our development study must state which mechanisms it implements, avoiding claims of reproducing an unimplemented three-layer interceptor.

methodological_corrections: A constant-label evaluator necessarily removes any accuracy difference. Its collapse is not evidence of oracle leakage; delete that proposed control.

A deterministic reference is valid for fully specified CPU tasks. Independence requires different implementation from the policy and no reference labels in its inputs, not a claim that all deterministic scoring is tautological.

A static import check or separate Python process does not establish a security sandbox. Describe the actual data-flow boundary and test it by changing private labels while holding public inputs fixed.
Do not infer workflow floor effects from the unrelated earlier huge-integer pilot. Preserve the negative pilot without further model capability calibration.
The ACM full-text limitation copied into the refiner output belongs to an earlier candidate and is not evidence about this arXiv-based proposal.

Specify a concrete difference between local repair, transitive invalidation and the proposed adapter before spending experiment calls. If identical, collapse the conditions and report the lack of a new mechanism.

Define failure persistence, clean and legitimate-update controls, all policies' observation access, tool-work allowance, and exact API call arithmetic. A prose maximum of six calls is not a cost decomposition.
Fixture/fault variants sharing one initial plan are paired repeated measures, not independent model samples. Reject-all is not successful completion.
